newsitem.title: MEXICO: MEXICO FIRST-HALF TAX RECEIPTS GROW 15 PCT - PAPER.
newsitem.headline: MEXICO FIRST-HALF TAX RECEIPTS GROW 15 PCT - PAPER.

text.p: Government tax receipts grew 15 percent in the first half compared to the same period a year ago, Mexico City financial daily El Economista said in its Monday editions.

Citing an advance copy of information from the Finance Ministry, El Economista said income tax revenues were up more than 18 percent against the first six months of 1996, and value added tax (VAT) revenues rose 14 percent.
El Economista said income tax receipts were 65.2 billion pesos in the first half and represented 40 percent of all tax revenues.

The newspaper said VAT receipts totaled 48.5 billion pesos and represented around 30 percent of ttotal revenues received by the Tax Administration System (SAT), which has replaced the Finance Ministry's revenues department.
Mexico's special tax on output and services, which is imposed on products such as cigarettes, was the third most important form of tax income.
The special tax generated income of 15.9 billion pesos in the first six half, a real decline of 10 percent from the first half of 1996, El Economista added.
The Finance Ministry is scheduled to present its quarterly financial report on Friday.
